Neurology 2005; 64: 1273–5. Treatment of Adverse Effects The stomach should be emptied by lavage if ingestion of ethyl- ene glycol was within the preceding hour. Severe metabolic aci- dosis should be corrected. Hypocalcaemia may require correc- tion with calcium gluconate in severe cases, although this is not usually done routinely because it may increase the formation of calcium oxalate crystals. Haemodialysis may be of value. Alco- hol may be given by mouth or intravenously as it is a competitor of the metabolism of ethylene glycol. Alternatively fomepizole (p.1446), an alcohol-dehydrogenase inhibitor, may be used for the treatment of ethylene glycol poisoning. ◊ References. 1. Harry P, et al. Ethylene glycol poisoning in a child treated with 4-methylpyrazole. Pediatrics 1998; 102: E31.
